name: One-time-priced session-prep kit for a single TTRPG system
buyer: Weekly or biweekly D&D or Pathfinder game master who dreads prep and subscription-tool stacks
pain: About four hours of prep for a two-hour session. One roundup says the tool stack can reach $60-150 per month, and another notes AI tools create tool fatigue.
wedge: A narrow prep kit for one system (e.g. Pathfinder 2e or one OSR game) at a one-time $29-39, with a prep-time target under 45 minutes. The notes doubt it beats funded competitors.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: A single-system kit with pre-structured prep output, targeting under 45 minutes. This is an unvalidated owner target.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If user tests show prep time above ~2 hours with the kit, or funded AI-for-DM tools already deliver the same reduction, there is no edge.

substitutesNoted.name: Roll20
substitutesNoted.price_point: Free tier; $5.99-$9.99/mo per one comparison (other sources conflict)

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: Model: one-time $29-39, ~55-65% margin per the owner's estimate after AI inference costs.

majorUncertainty: Whether a solo entrant can differentiate in the most crowded of the four markets, where many AI-for-DM tools launched in 2026.
unknowns: Whether the one-time pricing preference translates into purchases
Whether the claimed prep reduction is achievable
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Wizards of the Coast content is a licensing risk, so stay with the SRD or system-neutral content. Depends on AI inference providers.
